# Tomato trials

This year's trial compares two varieties of tomato side by side: an old heirloom and a modern hybrid. Both sit in the same bed, get the same water and the same feed, so that the variety is the only variable. One extra plant of the heirloom stays unstaked as the control.

I weigh the harvest every week and note the first ripe fruit, the split fruits and the taste on a scale of one to five. A trial needs a full season before anything is concluded. Do not change two things at once, or the result teaches nothing.

At the end of September I write down the winner and plan next year's comparison.
